title: Selective capability translation toward subnational sustainability transformation: Evidence from Vietnamese provinces
content:
by Anh Lan Nguyen, Chung Xuan Le

Progress toward subnational sustainability transformation depends not simply on whether provinces possess institutional and innovation capabilities, but on how those capabilities are associated with governance, economic performance, and broader sustainability outcomes. The analysis covered all 63 Vietnamese provinces and centrally governed cities from 2021 to 2023 (189 province-year observations). Six province-level domains were specified as formative composites in a partial least squares structural equation model, complemented by predictive, panel, outcome-specification, and regional robustness analyses. Institutional quality was associated most clearly with responsible public governance (β = 0.489), whereas innovation-enabling capacity was positively associated with regulatory–administrative quality, responsible public governance, and provincial economic performance. Provincial economic performance had the largest direct association with sustainable development outcomes (β = 0.549), and innovation-enabling capacity had a positive indirect association with the sustainability outcome through economic performance (β = 0.253). Regulatory–administrative quality was negatively associated with responsible public governance, while the institutional-quality interaction was not statistically significant. When the economic pillar was excluded from the sustainability composite, the economic-performance path and the corresponding indirect path remained significant (β = 0.473 and 0.221), although both estimates were smaller. Several pooled associations also weakened under fixed effects, and prediction was not systematically superior to a linear benchmark. The estimates therefore locate selective rather than uniform capability translation across provincial domains, while the short observational panel limits causal, temporal, and forecasting claims.
